findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_my_application, get_my_requests, update_my_application · Private data: find_products, get_next_steps, get_my_document_link, remove_my_document, list_my_applications, get_my_requests, get_request_file, mark_request_done, get_my_documents, upload_document, update_my_application, remove_from_my_application · Public sink: estimate_refinance_break_even, start_application, message_my_broker, upload_document, update_my_application · Destructive: check_servicing, add_to_shortlist, remove_from_shortlist, remove_my_document, remove_from_my_application.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_my_application, get_my_requests, update_my_application · Private data: find_products, get_next_steps, get_my_document_link, remove_my_document, list_my_applications, get_my_requests, get_request_file, mark_request_done, get_my_documents, upload_document, update_my_application, remove_from_my_application · Public sink: estimate_refinance_break_even, start_application, message_my_broker, upload_document, update_my_application · Destructive: check_servicing, add_to_shortlist, remove_from_shortlist, remove_my_document, remove_from_my_application

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
